cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, about the Midianites, the people the LORD said had deceived Israel in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:16-18). He gives Moses an assignment: "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites." And then, friend, He tells Moses something about Moses himself.

cards.question: After Moses takes vengeance on the Midianites, what does the LORD say will happen to him?

answers.text: He will be gathered to his people
He will cross over the Jordan
He will be made king of Israel

cards.text: So Moses tells the people to arm some of their men to go execute the LORD's vengeance on Midian. Not the whole camp, though. He's got a number in mind.

cards.question: Moses says to send ___ men from each tribe of Israel into battle.
A thousand men from each tribe of Israel makes an army of twelve thousand armed for war.

cards.text: Moses sends them into battle, and with them goes Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas doesn't show up empty-handed.

cards.question: What does Phinehas take with him into battle?

answers.text: The sanctuary vessels and signal trumpets
The ark of the covenant and Aaron's staff
The priestly robes and the anointing oil

cards.text: They wage war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they kill every male, including Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. And hold on, friend, because there's one more name on that list you've heard before in Numbers.

cards.question: Besides the five kings of Midian, who else is killed with the sword?

cards.text: The Israelites capture the Midianite women and their children. And the herds, the flocks, the goods? They plunder all of it.

cards.question: With the people and goods taken, what do the Israelites do to the Midianite cities and encampments?
The army carries away all the plunder, both people and animals. Where do they bring it?

answers.text: To the camp on the plains of Moab

cards.text: Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders head outside the camp to meet the army. But friend, this is no welcome-home party, because Moses is angry with the officers, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.

cards.question: Moses is angry with the army's officers. What does he ask them?

answers.text: If they spared all the women
Why they killed the five kings
Where Phinehas had gone off to

cards.text: Moses points back to Peor, in Numbers 25. He says these women, through the counsel of Balaam, the man Balak king of Moab once called to curse Israel (Numbers 22:4-6), caused the sons of Israel to turn unfaithfully against the LORD.

cards.question: Moses says that because of what happened at Peor, a ___ struck the congregation of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses gives an order that's hard to read, friend, and I'm not going to soften it: kill all the boys, and every woman who has had relations with a man. Every girl who never has is to be spared.
The soldiers are back from Midian, but they can't just stroll into camp. Moses says anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead has to stay outside the camp first.

cards.question: How long must anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead stay outside the camp?
On the third day and the seventh day, the soldiers purify themselves and their captives too.

cards.text: Moses adds every garment, leather good, goat's hair item and wooden article to the cleanup list. Then Eleazar the priest shares the LORD's statute for the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead.

cards.question: Eleazar says the metal that can withstand the fire is made clean how?

answers.text: It is buried for seven days
It is offered on the altar

cards.question: Eleazar also has a rule for everything that can't withstand the fire. What happens to it?

answers.text: It must pass through the water
It must be burned outside the camp
It must be left behind in Midian

cards.text: Even the metal that went through the fire still gets the water of purification. On the seventh day the soldiers wash their clothes, they're clean, and they can come back into camp.
Then the LORD tells Moses, Eleazar the priest and the family heads to count everything captured, both people and animals. After that, they're to divide it into two halves.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to divide the captives into two halves. Who gets them?

answers.text: The soldiers and the rest of the congregation
The Levites and the twelve tribes of Israel
The commanders and the heads of the families

cards.text: Then the LORD sets aside shares from both halves. From the soldiers' half, one out of every five hundred goes to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's tribute, and from the congregation's half, one out of every fifty goes to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle.

Moses and Eleazar do as the LORD commanded and count it all: 675,000 sheep, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys and 32,000 women. They split it in half, with the LORD's tribute and the Levites' share set aside, just as the LORD said.
Then the commanders of thousands and of hundreds come to Moses with a report. They've counted every soldier under their command.

cards.question: After counting the soldiers under their command, how many do the commanders say are missing?
The commanders bring the LORD an offering of the gold each man acquired. What do they say it's for?

answers.text: To pay for the army's weapons
To thank Moses for leading them

cards.text: Moses and Eleazar receive all the gold articles, and they weigh 16,750 shekels. And the text adds that each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.

cards.question: Where do Moses and Eleazar bring the commanders' gold, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD?

answers.text: Up to the top of Mount Nebo
Across to the city of Jericho

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 6 of the stop's 9 choice cards, with 2 fill in the blank and only 1 true or false. One type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 7 of the stop's 8 choice cards, with 1 true or false and no fill in the blank. Stop 2 also repeats stop 1's pattern of mostly multiple choice.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. It covers the lighter moments that could hold a laugh without muddying a fact: the purification of every garment and pot, the count of 675,000 sheep, and the commanders' report that not one soldier is missing. Instead, the cards read as flat narration. Stop 1 is a heavy stretch where restraint fits, but stop 2 gives up chances for laughs that suit the moment.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "There's one more name on that list you've heard before in Numbers" assumes the baker has read or done earlier lessons on Numbers. Papa Dorin isn't told that.

rule.text: What he doesn't know: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before. In lessons, he's never told, because every baker gets the same lesson.

findings.problem: Balaam first shows up in the card 8 teaser and the card 9 answer, but nothing says who he is until card 15. The introduction should come with his first appearance, for example right after card 9 is answered.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No earlier card says where Israel is camped, so the baker can only guess between the plains of Moab, Shiloh and Gilead. The stop already has several discovery questions (cards 4, 7 and 16). Either a story card should set up the camp's location, or the card should ask something the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The question is about things that can't withstand fire, so the wrong answer "It must be burned outside the camp" contradicts the question itself. It isn't believable and is easy to rule out.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: "The LORD sets aside shares from both halves" credits the setting aside to the LORD. In Numbers 31:28-30, the LORD commands Moses to set aside the tribute and the Levites' share.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
